from manim import *
import numpy as np

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section1Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Prerequisites: The Geometry of Sine Powers", [
            "We start with the integral of sine power.",
            "This area flattens as n increases.",
            "Visualizing sine powers as shrinking curves."
        ])
        
        axes = Axes(x_range=[0, 1.6, 0.5], y_range=[0, 1.2, 0.5], axis_config={"include_tip": False})
        axes.set_height(3)
        self.place_in_area(axes, 'B1', 'E3', scale_factor=0.6)
        
        # Assets
        compass = SVGMobject("/scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/compass.svg")
        calculator = SVGMobject("/scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/calculator.svg")
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color(BLUE)
        self.place_at_grid(compass, 'A1', scale_factor=0.5)
        curve1 = axes.plot(lambda x: np.sin(x), x_range=[0, 1.57], color=YELLOW)
        label1 = MathTex(r"I_n = \int_0^{\pi/2} \sin^n(x) dx").scale(0.6)
        self.place_at_grid(label1, 'A3', scale_factor=0.8)
        self.play(FadeIn(compass), Create(curve1), Write(label1))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.lecture[1].set_color(GREEN)
        curve2 = axes.plot(lambda x: np.sin(x)**10, x_range=[0, 1.57], color=RED)
        self.play(Transform(curve1, curve2))
        
        formula = MathTex(r"I_n = \frac{n-1}{n} I_{n-2}").scale(0.6)
        self.place_at_grid(formula, 'E5', scale_factor=0.9)
        self.play(Write(formula))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.lecture[2].set_color(ORANGE)
        self.place_at_grid(calculator, 'F5', scale_factor=0.5)
        # Visualizing the flattening
        self.play(Indicate(curve1), FadeIn(calculator))
        self.wait(1)

class Section2Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Deriving the Ratio: The Key Insight", [
            "Consider the ratio of consecutive integrals.", 
            "As n grows, this ratio nears one.", 
            "The gap between curves eventually vanishes."
        ])
        
        # Setup visual elements
        ratio_expr = MathTex(r"\frac{I_{2n+1}}{I_{2n}} \to 1").set_color(BLUE)
        ruler = SVGMobject("/scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/ruler.svg").set_color(BLUE)
        microscope = SVGMobject("/scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/microscope.svg").set_color(YELLOW)
        
        # Applying layout fixes from feedback
        self.place_at_grid(ratio_expr, 'B5', scale_factor=1.0)
        self.place_at_grid(ruler, 'A3', scale_factor=0.5)
        
        # Visualize gap
        gap_visual = VGroup(
            Line(UP, DOWN).set_color(YELLOW),
            Line(UP, DOWN).set_color(YELLOW).shift(RIGHT * 0.5)
        )
        self.place_in_area(gap_visual, 'D3', 'E5', scale_factor=0.6)
        self.place_at_grid(microscope, 'F5', scale_factor=0.5)
        
        ratio_expr.set_opacity(0)
        ruler.set_opacity(0)
        gap_visual.set_opacity(0)
        microscope.set_opacity(0)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color(BLUE)
        self.play(FadeIn(ruler), Write(ratio_expr))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[1].set_color(GREEN)
        self.play(ratio_expr.animate.set_color(GREEN))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.lecture[1].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[2].set_color(YELLOW)
        self.play(FadeIn(gap_visual), FadeIn(microscope), run_time=1)
        self.play(gap_visual.animate.shift(RIGHT * 0.5), run_time=1)
        self.play(gap_visual.animate.shift(LEFT * 0.5), run_time=1)
        self.wait(1)

class Section3Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = [
            "The Wallis product formula emerges here.",
            "Fractions multiply towards pi over two.",
            "Wallis-Bot assembles this infinite product.",
            "Output values converge to pi halves.",
            "Infinite steps reveal the target value."
        ]
        self.setup_layout("The Wallis Product Formula", lecture_lines)
        
        # Math objects
        wallis_expr = MathTex(
            r"{\pi \over 2} = \prod_{n=1}^{\infty} \left( {2n \over 2n-1} \cdot {2n \over 2n+1} \right)",
            font_size=36
        )
        self.place_in_area(wallis_expr, 'A3', 'C6', scale_factor=0.6)
        
        # Asset for robot
        robot_asset = "/scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/robot.svg"
        bot = SVGMobject(robot_asset, color=WHITE)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(YELLOW))
        self.play(Write(wallis_expr))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(BLUE))
        fraction_group = MathTex(
            r"\left( {2 \over 1} \cdot {2 \over 3} \right) \left( {4 \over 3} \cdot {4 \over 5} \right) \cdots",
            font_size=30
        )
        self.place_at_grid(fraction_group, 'D5', scale_factor=0.7)
        self.play(Write(fraction_group))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(GREEN))
        self.place_at_grid(bot, 'E4', scale_factor=0.8)
        self.play(FadeIn(bot))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[3].animate.set_color(ORANGE))
        display = DecimalNumber(1.0, num_decimal_places=4, color=WHITE)
        self.place_at_grid(display, 'F4', scale_factor=0.8)
        self.play(Write(display))
        self.play(display.animate.set_value(1.5707))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[4].animate.set_color(PURPLE))
        self.play(Indicate(wallis_expr))
        self.wait(1)

class Section5Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Summary & Real-World Significance", [
            "Recapping integrals, ratios, and products.", 
            "Historical approximations enabled complex calculations.", 
            "Pi builds from infinite fractional layers."
        ])
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Show Wallis Product formula segments
        formula = MathTex(r"\frac{\pi}{2} = \prod_{n=1}^{\infty} \left( \frac{4n^2}{4n^2-1} \right)", color=BLUE)
        self.place_in_area(formula, 'A2', 'B4', scale_factor=0.9)
        calculator = SVGMobject("/scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/calculator.svg", color=WHITE)
        self.place_at_grid(calculator, 'A5', scale_factor=0.5)
        self.lecture[0].set_color(BLUE)
        self.play(Write(formula), FadeIn(calculator))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        stat_text = Text("Utility: Probability & Statistics", font_size=20, color=YELLOW)
        self.place_at_grid(stat_text, 'C2', scale_factor=0.7)
        self.lecture[1].set_color(YELLOW)
        self.play(FadeIn(stat_text))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Build Pi from fractions
        pi_target = MathTex(r"\pi", font_size=72, color=GREEN)
        self.place_at_grid(pi_target, 'E4', scale_factor=1.0)
        coin = SVGMobject("/scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/coin.svg", color=GOLD)
        self.place_at_grid(coin, 'E5', scale_factor=0.5)
        self.lecture[2].set_color(GREEN)
        
        fracs = VGroup(*[
            MathTex(r"\frac{2}{1} \cdot \frac{2}{3} \cdot \frac{4}{3} \cdot \frac{4}{5} \dots", color=WHITE, font_size=24)
            for _ in range(3)
        ])
        
        for i, f in enumerate(fracs):
            self.place_at_grid(f, f'D{i+2}', scale_factor=0.8)
            self.play(FadeIn(f))
        
        self.play(Write(pi_target), FadeIn(coin))
        self.wait(2)

outline.topic: The Wallis Product: An Infinite Dance Toward Pi

sections.title: Prerequisites: The Geometry of Sine Powers
sections.content: Introduce the integral of sin^n(x) from 0 to π/2. Explain the reduction formula (Wallis Integrals) visually as the area under a curve that 'flattens' as n increases.
sections.example: Visualize the area shrinking: compare sin^1(x) (quarter-circle curve) to sin^10(x) (a thin spike hugging the y-axis).

sections.title: Deriving the Ratio: The Key Insight
sections.content: Show the ratio of two consecutive Wallis integrals, I_{2n+1} / I_{2n}. Explain that as n approaches infinity, this ratio approaches 1. This is the foundation for isolating π.
sections.example: An animated 'tug-of-war' between two shrinking shapes where the gap between them eventually vanishes.

sections.title: The Wallis Product Formula
sections.content: Reveal the infinite product formula: π/2 = (2/1 * 2/3) * (4/3 * 4/5) * (6/5 * 6/7) .... Connect the algebraic terms to the limiting process derived in the previous section.
sections.example: A mechanical assembly line where a robot (let's name him 'Wallis-Bot') repeatedly multiplies fractions, with the output value slowly converging to 1.5707... on a digital display.

sections.title: Intuition: Why Pi?
sections.content: Discuss why this infinite product involves only integers. Explain the 'beauty' of infinite series/products—taking discrete rational numbers and arriving at the transcendental constant π.
sections.example: A 'Pixel-Cat' character trying to measure a circular yarn ball; each fraction in the product represents one step of the cat tracing the circumference.

sections.title: Summary & Real-World Significance
sections.content: Recap: Wallis Integrals -> Ratio -> Infinite Product. Mention how such approximations were historically vital for calculation before modern supercomputers.
sections.example: A closing animation showing the number 'π' being built like a scaffold, layer by layer, out of infinitely many floating numerical fractions.
